findings.description: The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. User-data is retrievable by principals with instance or launch-template access and can be exposed through host compromise, source control, Terraform state, or EC2 metadata/user-data access.

TCP/22 is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0. Because the instance is placed in a subnet routed to an internet gateway with automatic public IP assignment, this exposes SSH authentication to the entire internet.

TCP/80 is exposed to 0.0.0.0/0 and the instance user-data installs and starts Apache without any TLS/HTTPS configuration. Requests and responses to the publicly reachable web service can therefore be transmitted in cleartext.
The security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromise of the internet-reachable instance can use unrestricted egress for command-and-control or data exfiltration.

The EBS volume has no encryption configuration or KMS key, so this Terraform configuration does not enforce encryption at rest and may create an unencrypted volume where account-level default encryption is not enabled.
The bucket that receives VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. The configuration therefore does not ensure encryption at rest for network-activity records stored in this archive.
